what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 4 of 4: The force of a slow wind on a capturing sphere: why K/K_0 falls from 1 at low density to 0.57 at density 0.75. SETTING (blocks 44 and 45; open PRs titled 'ail44: records with inertia' and 'ail45: the wind law'): a supplied clause, not adopted: a record's content is its direction of travel; (S) a record steps along its content (sphere menu: to x + e_k with probability max(0, s.e_k)/sqrt 3), an occupied target exchanges contents with it, a solid site reflects it or, if the body CAPTURES, keeps it; (C) each bond at rate gamma re-draws its pair of contents uniformly on their momentum class. PROVED: number and momentum conserved by every event with explicit local current and momentum flux; the uniform measure is stationary; product states have mass current (1 - rho) g/sqrt 3 and pressure rho/(3 sqrt 3) (sphere menu), wave speed squared (1 - rho)/9; the second-order momentum flux is sqrt3 Pi_ij = (rho/3) delta_ij + A g_i g_j + B g^2 delta_ij with A = (3/5 - rho)/rho, B = -1/(5 rho); from the second-order flux alone (the INVISCID value) the force of a uniform wind g1 on a body drawing the inflow q is A q g1 = (3/5 - rho)/(1 - rho) times the simple estimate Q2 g1/rho (sign change at rho = 3/5); in free streaming it is exactly the simple estimate, K_0 = sqrt3/(4 pi rho (1 - rho)) in F = K Q1 Q2/r^2. EXECUTED (side 96, gamma 1 unless said): the wind around one capturing body equals sqrt3 Q <1/r^2>/(4 pi (1 - rho)) within 0.974 to 1.003 from r = 7 to 32 with the density flat; two capturing bodies attract with F = K Q1 Q2/r^2, symmetric in the two bodies, K = 0.49 to 0.72 at density 0.3; K/K_0 = 1.02, 1.0, 0.72, 0.57 at density 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75 (NO sign change) and 1.13, 0.87 at gamma = 0.1, 4: the executed flows have Reynolds numbers below 0.1 and do not follow the inviscid value; the capture rate is NOT the record count for dense bodies (a ball with a tenth of its sites captures 43 per cent of the full ball; Q grows like the square of the radius). Simulators: probes/lib/inertial.py and probes/lib/inertial_bodies.py (see their docstrings); porous bodies need the constructor changed as described in the task. TASK: block 45 has two computed values of K = F r^2/(Q1 Q2): K_0 (free streaming: a body takes up the mean momentum of what it captures) and K_0 (3/5 - rho)/(1 - rho) (inviscid, from the second-order flux alone), and the executed K/K_0 = 1.02, 1.0, 0.72, 0.57 at density 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.13, 0.87 at gamma = 0.1, 4, at Reynolds numbers below 0.1. Explain the executed numbers. (a) Set up the linearized kinetic (relaxation-time) equation of the clause around a uniform wind for the sphere menu: streaming with exclusion in the product closure plus scattering (C) at rate gamma relaxing the second moment of the contents; solve for the flow past an absorbing sphere of radius R at small wind and obtain the force as a function of the ratio of the mean free path to R. (b) Identify the regime of the executed runs (viscous: the net force is carried to the far field by viscous stress at first order in the wind) and give the force on an absorbing sphere there: the depletion of the gas near the body, the perturbation of the wind at its surface, and the resulting K/K_0 as a function of rho, gamma and R. (c) Say at what Reynolds number the inviscid value, with its sign change at rho = 3/5, should appear, and whether any executable run could reach it. State what is exact and what is a closure. check.py: the relaxation rates of the second moments under (C), exactly (the scattering kernel on the momentum class).  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/wind-force-on-an-absorbing-sphere/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route.
